text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- On the occasion of his annual New Year's Day speech President Arpad Goncz explained the need for the austerity measures of the past two years and said they have brought Hungary out of economic crisis. @
- Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti has dismissed deputy state secretary Laszlo Borsits.
- The Providencia insurance company has outbid 11 other companies to win a tender launched by the Interior Ministry to insure all professional ministry staff in 1997.
- A rocket hit the second floor of a building on Buda's Szepvolgyi ut just after midnight New Year's Eve, causing HUF 300,000 damage, but injuring no-one.
- As many as 63 snow clearance machines were at work in Budapest yesterday as 1997 began with a heavy dousing of snow.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- An editorial comment observes that 1997 could be described as a key year, as it directly precedes the election year of 1998, when it will be seen whether the present coalition can hang on or it will cede its place to the opposition.

- Customs rates on imported goods went down by 2 percent to 2-3 percent on average yesterday, and the 1 percent customs and statistical charge on products imported from countries of the World Trade Organisation has been abolished.
- The average yield at the December 31 auction of one-month treasury bills slipped down by just 0.04 to 28.84 percent. @
- The 1996 loss of the national railway company MAV Rt. will exceed the projected HUF 9.4 billion by HUF 4.5-5 billion.

- A senior executive of Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank of Germany confirmed that the institution will tender an offer to buy Hungary's Takarekbank, the bank of 250 savings cooperatives, when a call for bids is made.
- The state bought back the ailing Polgari Bank from US investors GE Capital in order to make sure that the bank can continue operations, said former privatisation minister Tamas Suchman. @
- Starting this year, small-scale agricultural producers are only allowed to sell their produce on markets if they possess a certificate issued by the state.
- The National Police will receive HUF 5 billion via a German loan for a general upgrade, including the purchase of about 2,000 new cars.
NEPSZABADSAG

- The reform of the Hungarian health care system has come to a halt, and World Bank money originally loaned for that purpose should perhaps be put to related uses, according to Guy Ellena of the Bank's Budapest office. @
- This paper reports that Austrian insurance company Grazer Wechselseitige, accused of mediating illegal insurance deals in the past, will receive a permit to operate in Hungary early this year.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- A chart shows what lies ahead on Hungary's economic front, as seen by analysts at Budapest Bank and economic research firms GKI and Kopint-Datorg. @
- The total turnover on the Budapest Commodity and Stock Exchanges came to an unprecedented HUF 1,672 billion, or over $10 billion, in 1996 which equals 25 percent of the country's GDP.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- As required by the new securities law, an Investor Protection Fund will be set up by July 1.
